requirements.evidence: Almost all requirements are implemented. Migration with FK cascade, nullable invited_by and unique (entity_id,email) (migration:14-25). Model setter normalizes email (EntityInvite.php `Str::lower(trim($value))`). sendInvite validates, rejects existing members and pending invites, replaces expired ones, turns unique violations into an inviteEmail error, rate-limits only successful sends (`RateLimiter::hit` after create), queues mail and writes an audit log (Members.php:46-125). PendingInvites accept/decline cover the 403, expired, idempotent and firstOrCreate cases. Modals use ui.members_details and ui.members_remove_title. The <hr> is conditional on invites. Mail strings and pt_BR JSON are added. Gaps: accepted invites are kept and only unaccepted expired rows are deleted (`->whereNull('accepted_at')->where('expires_at','<=',now())->delete()`), so a removed member can never be re-invited. The UI also relies on `UserRole::manageable()`, `ui.email` and `ui.name`, which are not in the diff.

conventions.evidence: Follows these: #[Validate] on inviteEmail/inviteRole/memberRole, a migration with a reversible down(), #[Fillable] on the model, Bulma modals, and docs/CHANGELOG updates (business-rules.md, database-schema.md, architecture.md). Deviations: domain writes (create invite, accept invite creating a membership, change role) stay inline in Livewire components instead of `app/Actions/*`. Invitee authorization is a hand-rolled `abort_unless(Str::lower($invite->email) === ...)` rather than a policy/`$this->authorize`. Server-only state `selectedMembershipId`/`confirmingRemoval` is not #[Locked]. The view contains an `@php` lookup block (members.blade.php:6-10).

security.evidence: Every manager action calls `$this->authorize('update', $this->entity)`. Parameters are resolved through entity-scoped relations (`$this->entity->invites()->findOrFail`, `$this->entity->memberships()->findOrFail($this->selectedMembershipId)`), so a tampered selectedMembershipId cannot reach another entity. mount requires update. accept/decline check the invitee's e-mail. The owner is excluded by `in:admin,employee`. The rate limiter is present, output is escaped with {{ }}, and mass assignment is explicit. Minor: there is no #[Locked] on selectedMembershipId, and closeMember/cancelRemoval are unauthorized (harmless state toggles).

tests.evidence: Good coverage: invite happy path with normalization and Mail::assertQueued, member/pending conflicts, expired replacement, quota not consumed by invalid input, rate limit at 10, employee 403 on both route and component, error rendered once, foreign membership ModelNotFound, saveRole owner/immutable/last-manager, confirmation flow, accept/decline/expired/idempotent/non-invitee, mail en+pt_BR, onboarding without <hr>. Missing: the existing test 'cannot remove the last manager of an entity' was deleted, and its replacement 'removing the owner or the last manager is forbidden' only checks the owner. No tamper test for cancelInvite with another entity's invite, no test of the unique-violation race path, and no test that a former member can be re-invited.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly direct. `isUniqueViolation()` hand-parses driver codes and message substrings ('unique','duplicate') where catching Laravel's `UniqueConstraintViolationException` would do. The model adds unused extras: `inviter()`, a booted default expiry, and isPending/isExpired, which are used only in tests. The `scopeForEmail` whereRaw lower() is redundant given the normalized storage.

readability.evidence: Clear names and focused methods, plus helpful comments (`// An expired invite may be replaced...`). sendInvite is long (~80 lines) with mixed concerns (validation, duplicate checks, rate limit, transaction, mail, audit). No debug output or dead code.

scope.evidence: Nearly everything serves the task. Small extras: a public `closeMember()` not in the contract, the `inviter()` relation, and rewording the database-schema.md intro ('Domain proposal — no migrations in this repository yet').

issues.explanation: Accepted invites are kept and only unaccepted expired rows are deleted before insert, so after a member is removed, re-inviting the same e-mail hits the unique (entity_id,email) index and wrongly reports 'already has a pending invite' forever.
The existing test that the last manager cannot be removed was deleted, and the renamed replacement only checks owner removal, so the 'never the last manager' removal rule is no longer covered.
Invite creation, invite acceptance (which creates a membership) and role changes are domain writes done inline in components instead of through app/Actions classes as the conventions require.
Invitee authorization is a hand-rolled abort_unless e-mail comparison instead of a policy/gate called through $this->authorize.
Server-only state selectedMembershipId and confirmingRemoval are not #[Locked]; the code re-scopes queries, so this is not exploitable, but it breaks the Livewire policy.
There is no tamper test for cancelInvite with an invite from another entity and no test of the unique-constraint race becoming an inviteEmail error.
The views depend on UserRole::manageable() and the ui.email/ui.name keys, none of which is added in the diff; if any is missing, the members page breaks.
isUniqueViolation sniffs driver codes and message substrings; catching Illuminate\Database\UniqueConstraintViolationException is simpler and more precise.
The expiry date uses toFormattedDateString(), which is always English, even in the pt_BR e-mail.

review.summary: The change replaces direct member adding with an invite flow: a migration, a model with e-mail normalization, a factory, a queued markdown mailable, a manager-only members page with detail and confirmation modals, and a PendingInvites component, plus docs and broad tests. Authorization and validation are solid, but a removed member can never be re-invited because accepted invite rows block the unique index. A last-manager removal test was dropped, and domain writes bypass the Actions/policy conventions, so it needs changes before merge.
